question: What is the UAE's current federal, Dubai, DIFC and ADGM legal and operating perimeter for payment tokens, virtual-asset services and Digital Dirham; which named legal persons, products, major banks and rails actually operate; and where do reserves, custody, finality, correction and customer loss remain?
bluf: The UAE has a layered regulatory architecture rather than one crypto licence: CBUAE owns payment tokens, Digital Dirham and licensed financial activities regardless of technology; SCA owns the federal investment-type VASP perimeter; VARA covers Dubai outside DIFC; DFSA covers DIFC; and FSRA covers ADGM. The live CBUAE register still names three Dirham Payment Token Issuance legal persons, while VARA's live register still shows 56 active fully licensed VASPs in its own Dubai perimeter. AE Coin, Zand AED and DDSC have product evidence; DDSC has one disclosed AED 110 million transaction. The major-bank layer is uneven: FAB is a DDSC founding participant and proposed customer-access channel but AEDC Stable Coin LLC is the registered issuer; Emirates NBD's Liv X operates retail crypto brokerage through VARA-licensed Aquanow with Zodia custody; ADCB has VASP risk controls but no verified customer crypto product; and DIB's Crypto.com work remains an exploratory MoU. Digital Dirham has bounded live government and UAE-China CBDC transactions, not proven general public circulation. UAEFTS remains the sovereign RTGS/finality anchor. No map route arc is yet authorized.

authority.summary: Federal law and Cabinet decisions establish the national frame. CBUAE owns payment-token services, Digital Dirham, technology-neutral licensed-financial-activity jurisdiction and payment-system oversight. SCA owns federal investment-type VAs and VASPs outside financial free zones. VARA covers Dubai outside DIFC, DFSA covers DIFC and FSRA covers ADGM. FTA owns tax; courts, insolvency office-holders and law enforcement own separate adjudication and recovery capacities.
authority.boundary: Federal, emirate, commercial-free-zone, financial-free-zone, payment-token, investment-product, tax, enforcement and settlement authorities are distinct and may overlap only through an express gate.

legal_objects.summary: The record separates sovereign AED and CBUAE settlement balances, Digital Dirham, licensed private Dirham Payment Tokens, registered Foreign Payment Tokens, investment-type virtual assets and Crypto Tokens, VASP customer assets, payment-token reserve assets, bank deposits and blockchain entries.
legal_objects.boundary: A common digital or blockchain form does not merge central-bank currency, private issuer debt, bank liability, investment right, custodied asset, reserve pool, chain state or final settlement entry.

permitted_activities.summary: CBUAE licences AED-token issuance and licences or registers payment-token conversion, custody and transfer. SCA, VARA, DFSA and FSRA licence or authorise location- and activity-specific investment and VASP services. Ordinary merchants may accept licensed Dirham Payment Tokens, while registered Foreign Payment Tokens are bounded to virtual-asset or derivative purchases. Algorithmic stablecoin and privacy-token issuance, service and promotion are prohibited in the CBUAE payment perimeter.
permitted_activities.boundary: Issuer, conversion, custody, broker, exchange, advisory, market, merchant-payment and promotion permissions attach to exact legal persons, activities, instruments and territories.

entry_gates.summary: Payment-token issuance requires a CBUAE licence; conversion and foreign-token custody may require CBUAE non-objection on top of SCA or local VASP status. VARA in-principle approval cannot operate or serve clients. DIFC and ADGM require their own DFSA or FSRA authorisation. Register inclusion and exact activity scope establish entry, not an application, marketing claim or group-company licence.
entry_gates.boundary: Application, IPA, non-objection, licence grant, effective date, product approval, launch, first transaction and recurring production each require separate evidence.

named_operating_actors.summary: The live CBUAE register names AED StableCoin L.L.C - S.P.C, Zand Trust L.L.C S.O.C and AEDC Stable Coin-L.L.C as Dirham Payment Token Issuance legal persons and AEDC Stable Coin Network And Distribution - L.L.C in conversion/custody and payment-service categories. VARA's cutoff register shows 56 active fully licensed VASPs in Dubai outside DIFC. AE Coin, AEDZ and DDSC have named product evidence. CBUAE's latest explicit public D-SIB population is FAB, Emirates NBD, ADCB and DIB; Zand is reviewed separately because its trust company is a registered issuer. Other federal and financial-free-zone rosters still need a joined cutoff export.
named_operating_actors.boundary: Legal person, group, licence, licence category, product brand, agent, network, active customer service and market scale are different facts.

claims_and_backing.summary: Payment-token holders have a par-redemption right without delay and no later than the same time on the next business day unless CBUAE permits otherwise. The default reserve is 100% same-currency cash in segregated escrow; a bank-owned issuer may hold at least 50% cash and the remainder in short-duration UAE government bonds or CBUAE M-bills. Daily reconciliation/reporting, monthly external audit and an insolvency claim against the reserve are required. Issuer-specific current balances and redemption performance remain open.
claims_and_backing.boundary: Statutory design, product statement, dated reserve balance, attestation, liquidity, redemption request, completed payment and insolvency recovery are separate evidence states.

domestic_rails.summary: UAEFTS is the CBUAE-owned RTGS and settles bank and financial-institution transfers individually in real time through central-bank accounts. Aani is an instant account-to-account retail rail. Digital Dirham/Jisr supplies bounded wholesale CBDC operation. Private payment-token networks sit upstream or alongside these sovereign and commercial-money records unless a specific settlement chain proves otherwise.
domestic_rails.boundary: Wallet display, VASP ledger, token transfer, reserve redemption, customer bank credit, Aani payment, Digital Dirham movement and UAEFTS final settlement are distinct clocks.

cross_border_routes.summary: The China-UAE joint statement records an AED 50 million first direct Digital Dirham payment with China through mBridge by 2 June 2024. CBUAE's later 19 November 2025 record establishes the Jisr launch and a transaction on that arrangement. The public evidence does not complete the exact 2024 transaction date, payer/payee and institutions, funding, FX, both currency legs, beneficiary credit, legal finality, correction or recurring bilateral series. DDSC's disclosed transfer does not name a foreign endpoint.
cross_border_routes.boundary: The 2025 Jisr event is not safely described as the first-ever bilateral CBDC payment; normalized endpoints and two official sides still do not authorize a route arc without the end-to-end chain.

operating_state.summary: Payment-token, VARA and financial-free-zone regimes are effective; UAEFTS and Aani are production rails. AE Coin and AEDZ present active issuer products. DDSC entered operational deployment in February 2026 and has one disclosed AED 110 million transfer in May. The bank-product review verifies Liv X retail crypto trading, with Aquanow providing brokerage infrastructure and Zodia custody; it does not make Emirates NBD the exchange or custodian. FAB participates in DDSC but the registered issuer is AEDC Stable Coin LLC. ADCB's disclosed VASP framework and blockchain analytics are bank-risk controls, not customer trading or custody. DIB's Crypto.com relationship is an exploratory MoU, while its 2026 Jaywan card is a conventional payment product. Digital Dirham has a bounded AED 50 million UAE-China mBridge payment disclosed in 2024, a domestic-government transaction and Jisr launch/transaction evidence in 2025, while general retail circulation remains unproved.
operating_state.boundary: Effective regime, licence, product page, approval to launch, first transaction, controlled government use, recurring production and general-purpose public circulation are different operating states.

scale.summary: The official cutoff measures are three CBUAE issuer legal persons, one named payment-token conversion/custody person, 56 active VARA VASPs, four D-SIBs, one AED 110 million DDSC transaction, 12.5 million Aani users, 74 connected Aani institutions and about 774,000 merchants. In 2025 UAEFTS processed 114.9 million retail transfers worth AED 9.9 trillion and 865,708 institutional transfers worth AED 14.5 trillion. Emirates NBD says group digital-wealth AUM almost tripled and trading volumes increased fourfold in 2025, but does not isolate Liv X crypto customers, balances or trades. Complete token, VASP and bank-product activity series are absent.
scale.boundary: Licence, user, merchant and conventional-rail counts do not establish crypto balances, customers, activity, solvency, reserve adequacy or recurring corridor volume.

stress.summary: CBUAE's 2026 thematic review and Payment Token Services Regulation identify material AML/CFT/CPF, technology and cross-border risks. VARA's June 2026 notices establish enforcement against unlicensed MEXC and KuCoin and a separate action concerning licensed CoinMENA. No joined official national series for licensed-provider hacks, customer losses, reserve runs, insolvencies or recoveries was located.
stress.boundary: Risk assessment, warning, fine, licence action, outage, compromise, quantified customer loss, insolvency, adjudication and recovery distribution are separate facts.

correction_and_loss.summary: Correction can occur through issuer mint/burn and redemption, agent/custodian/VASP books, chain controls or compensating transfers, bank and payment-system processes, regulatory restrictions, and court or insolvency action. Federal law protects qualifying infrastructure settlement as final and irreversible, while payment-token customers hold a separate reserve-backed contractual claim. No complete loss-allocation and recovery series was found.
correction_and_loss.boundary: Technical reversal, ledger correction, token burn, par redemption, licence suspension, fine, reserve claim, confiscation, adjudication and customer restitution have separate clocks.

evidence_boundary.summary: The recertification uses current CBUAE, SCA, VARA, DFSA, ADGM, FTA, bank and ADX-hosted disclosures and retains existing Workbench owners as bounded context. It separates regulatory registers, issuer statements, one disclosed transaction, sovereign rails, bank products, outsourced regulated roles and future claims and carries no route arc. The post-15 September sweep found no substantive crypto-regime, issuer, launch or transaction change through the intraday cutoff.
evidence_boundary.boundary: Fresh research is not Chronicle promotion, publication authority, investment advice, watch creation, app shipment, a generated-file editing permission or proof of a recurring crypto corridor.
